name: subsidence
job: Forecast how far each spot will have sunk at the next NISAR Pass
user: City water and infrastructure planners watching where the ground sinks fastest

labels.source: The site's own GUNW time series; Passes 2026-09-19, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-13 held out
labels.notes: Scores measure how well the next Passes are forecast, not ground truth from levelling or GNSS

baseline.name: Straight-line extrapolation of each pixel's history

model.name: LightGBM correction of the straight line

split: Time split: trained on forecasts ending by 2026-09-07, tested on the next 3 Passes; validation origin 2026-07-21 (Model 0.767 cm, Baseline 0.751 cm)
limits: Does not beat the straight-line Baseline: use the Baseline forecast; the Model is shown for transparency
Under one year of data, so seasonal swings (groundwater pumping, rain) cannot be learned
Errors include the atmospheric noise of each interferogram, which no forecast can predict
Line-of-sight displacement only; vertical sinking is assumed to dominate in Mexico City
The displacement sign (toward or away from the satellite) is our reading of the product; ASF has not yet confirmed it
